chunks: Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Muhammad ibn Salim, from Ahmad ibn al-Nadr, from 'Amr ibn Shimr, from Jabir, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) ate the eating of a slave and sat the sitting of a slave, and he (peace be upon him and his family) ate on the low ground and slept on the low ground.
ai.seo_question: How did the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family) demonstrate humility in his daily habits of eating and sleeping?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi underscores the Prophet’s (peace be upon him) adherence to the Sunnah of humility, illustrating that his modesty in eating and sleeping on the ground was not a sign of low status but a deliberate embodiment of servitude to God. In Shia tradition, this is often contrasted with the regal bearing of the Imams, highlighting the Prophet's unique role as the perfect servant (Abd) whose simplicity served as a practical lesson in detachment from worldly luxury.
